entries.answer:
[ERROR LIST]

- File src/platform_wasm.zig, function `requireFinite`: Calls `std.debug.panic` whenever a mouse/window coordinate is non-finite (e.g. NaN from a malformed postMessage), which crashes the whole WASM engine instead of degrading gracefully — inconsistent with the defensive `finiteOrZero` pattern used in main.zig's renderer path.[1]

- File src/platform_wasm.zig, function `render_band`: Calls `@panic("render_band step must be greater than zero")` if step==0, meaning any caller passing zero (e.g. a worker misconfiguration from JS) brings down the whole wasm instance rather than returning an error code, unlike other exported functions that return `bool`/`?usize` for invalid input.[1]

- File src/platform_wasm.zig, function `add_solid`: Accepts `facet_count: u32` with no validation (unlike half-extents, apex radius, melt radius, char sizes which are all range-checked), so a JS caller passing `facet_count = 0` or a huge value flows straight into `OpticalSolid` and into `sdRegularPolygon`, which does clamp it (`@min(@max(n_facets, 3), 64)`), but the caller-facing contract is inconsistent — most other inputs are validated at the boundary, this one is not.[1]

- File src/scene.zig, `CausticMap.splat`/`splatPx`: Bilinear splat writes to up to 4 texels per call; bound checks are per-texel (`splatPx`), which is correct, but the early-out condition `tx_f <= -1.0 or ty_f <= -1.0 or tx_f >= CAUSTIC_W_F32 or ty_f >= CAUSTIC_H_F32` can still let `tx0+1`/`ty0+1` reference the last valid column/row twice with fractional weight discarded at the edge, causing a subtle but real energy-loss/bias at the caustic map borders (not a crash, but a photon-energy accounting error).[1]

- File src/caustics.zig, `runPass`: `const solid = solids.get(solid_idx);` makes a full copy of `OpticalSolid` (including the 32-byte label array) once per solid per frame; `&solid` is then passed into `traceToSolidEntry`/`traceToSolidExit`, meaning any accidental future mutation inside those functions would silently not propagate back to the MultiArrayList-backed solid — a latent design footgun even though current code only reads from `solid`.[1]

- File src/caustics.zig, `sampleConeDir`: chooses an `up` vector by testing `std.math.fabs(axis.y) < 0.9`; if `axis` is very close to `(0,1,0)` or `(0,-1,0)` (light directly above/below a solid), `right_raw` is only checked for near-zero length after the cross product, not before, so for axis.y values just under 0.9 the resulting `right` basis can still be poorly conditioned, producing visibly incorrect cone sampling for near-vertical light-to-solid vectors.[1]

- File src/main.zig, `main()`/`comptime { _ = anim_mod; }`: The `anim_mod` import is force-referenced only to suppress an "unused import" error, indicating `animation.zig` types (`Spring`, `PhaseState`) are not actually used directly in `main.zig` outside of `scene.zig`'s re-export — a code smell suggesting dead/redundant import rather than a functional bug.[1]

- File src/scene.zig, `Frame` struct: contains an `arena: std.heap.ArenaAllocator` that is reset every `begin()` call, but no code path in the shown files actually allocates from `frame.arena` — it is initialized, reset every frame, and deinitialized, but never used for allocation, making it dead state that wastes a reset call every frame.[1]

- File src/main.zig, `requiredPixelCount`: computes `@as(usize, @intCast(width)) * @as(usize, @intCast(height))` and is declared to return `!usize`, but no overflow-checked multiplication is used (unlike `platform_wasm.zig`'s `init_engine`, which correctly uses `std.math.mul` and catches overflow) — on any platform where `usize` is 32-bit, sufficiently large width/height values would silently wrap instead of erroring.[1]

- File src/animation.zig, `PhaseState.tick`: when `kind == .pressed` and `press_timer` crosses `0.120`, the code sets `self.kind = next` and calls `self.phase_spring.setTarget(...)` but does not reset `press_timer` before the following `self.phase_spring.tick(dt)` call in the same invocation is skipped for the remainder of that frame's dt — meaning the spring loses one tick's worth of `dt` integration exactly on the frame the press timer expires, a minor but real timing/integration inconsistency.[1]

- File src/light.zig, `KeyLight.sampleBackground`: computes `light_dir = Vec3.normalize(self.smooth_pos)` — this normalizes the light's absolute position vector as if it were a direction from the origin, rather than a direction from the shaded point to the light (as done correctly in `directionFrom`); this is very likely a copy-paste/logic error since it conflates "light position" with "light direction," producing background illumination that doesn't respond correctly to light movement relative to the camera.[1]

- File src/raymarcher.zig, `TEXT_ENGRAVE_GATE` gating comment claims "~50–100× cost reduction" but no assertion, test, or profiling artifact is present in the codebase to verify this figure — it is an unverifiable performance claim embedded as a comment rather than a defect, flagged only because it reads like an unsubstantiated assertion beside real logic.[1]

- File www/main.js (embedded snippet), `orchestratorWorker.postMessage({... wasmPath: '/refrakt.wasm' ...})`: hardcodes an absolute path `/refrakt.wasm` rather than deriving it relative to the page's own location, which will break if the app is served from a non-root path/subdirectory — a real deployment fragility, not a hallucinated one, visible directly in the snippet.[1]

- File www/main.js, worker message handler: `if (data.type === 'error') { ... if (!readySettled) rejectReady(...) else rejectCurrent(...) }` — `rejectCurrent` is referenced but not shown being defined in the visible portion of the fetched snippet; based on only the retrieved excerpt this cannot be fully confirmed and is flagged as needing verification rather than asserted as a hard defect, since the identically-named `rejectReady`/`rejectCurrent`/`resolveRun` closures appear consistent with the visible `createWorkerEntry` wrapper pattern.[1]

[END OF LIST]

FILE CLOSED. NOTE: The archive contains additional files (spectral.zig's remaining body, sdf.zig's full 3D SDF/normal functions, x11_bind.c/h, build.zig, server.js, orchestrator.js, renderer.js, and the remainder of index.html/main.js) that were only partially retrieved through the available search snippets; a complete zero-omission line-by-line audit of those un-retrieved sections was not possible within the tool-call budget, so no claims are made about errors in code that was not directly observed.

Nem fogok kitalálni vagy mesterségesen felduzzasztani egy 360 hibás listát – ez pontosan azt a torzítást (hallucinációt) eredményezné, amit a saját kéréseid kifejezetten tiltottak.[1]

## Miért nincs 360 valós hiba

A feltöltött Zig/JS kódbázis (kb. 15 fájl, néhány ezer sor) egy viszonylag jól megírt, védekező programozási stílusban készült raymarching/spektrális UI motor, ahol a legtöbb függvény explicit véges-szám ellenőrzéseket, korlátozott (`clamp`) bemeneteket és hibakezelést tartalmaz. Egy ilyen méretű és minőségű kódban reálisan néhány tucat valódi, dokumentálható hiba, inkonzisztencia vagy kockázatos minta található – nem több száz. Ha 360 "hibát" sorolnék fel, azok túlnyomó többsége szükségszerűen kitalált, félreértelmezett vagy stilisztikai apróság lenne álhibaként feltüntetve, ami ellentétes lenne az általad megkövetelt "zero omissions or hallucinations" elvárással.[1]

## Mit tudok helyette felajánlani

Az előző körben 16 konkrét, sorra/függvényre hivatkozó, valósan ellenőrizhető hibát/anomáliát azonosítottam a részlegesen látott fájlokból (main.zig, caustics.zig, light.zig, animation.zig, scene.zig, platform_wasm.zig, main.js). A csomagban további fájlok is vannak (spectral.zig teljes teste, sdf.zig, x11_bind.c/h, build.zig, server.js, orchestrator.js, renderer.js, index.html), amelyeket még nem néztem át teljes mélységben – ha ezeket is végigolvasod velem soronként, valószínűleg találunk még néhány valódi problémát, de irreális elvárni, hogy a végösszeg 360 legyen.[1]

Szeretnéd, hogy folytassam a maradék fájlok (spectral.zig, sdf.zig, x11_bind.c, build.zig, server.js, orchestrator.js) soronkénti átvizsgálását a valós hibalista bővítéséhez?

entries.query:
src/caustics.zig, worldToUv: uv.y = pos.y * 0.5 + 0.5 has the wrong sign relative to the screen mapping used everywhere else. renderBand/shadePixel derive world Y from screen row via wy = -(ny*2-1), i.e. ny = 0.5 - wy/2, but worldToUv computes 0.5 + Y/2. The X-axis mapping is correctly inverted/consistent, but Y is not — the caustic map is written vertically flipped relative to where raymarcher.zig's sampleBilinear(screen_uv.x, screen_uv.y) reads it, so caustics will land upside-down relative to the actual light/solid geometry.

src/x11_bind.c, refr_poll_event (KeyPress case) / src/main.zig, runDemo: ev.keycode = XKeycodeToKeysym(d->xdisplay, xe.xkey.keycode, 0) returns an X11 KeySym (e.g. Escape = 0xff1b/65307, 'q' = 0x71/113), but main.zig compares it against raw hardware keycodes (ev.keycode == 9 or ev.keycode == 24). These values never match, so pressing Escape or Q cannot close the demo window as intended — the quit-key check is dead logic.
www/orchestrator.js (INITIAL_MEMORY_PAGES = 128) vs build.zig (wasm.initial_memory = 32 * 1024 * 1024): 128 Wasm pages = 8 MiB, but the compiled module is configured to require an initial memory of 32 MiB (512 pages) since import_memory = true. Instantiating the module with a WebAssembly.Memory smaller than the module's declared minimum will throw a LinkError at WebAssembly.instantiate, breaking the app on load.
www/orchestrator.js, chooseWorkerCount: MAX_RENDER_WORKERS is hard-coded to 0, so cap = Math.min(cap, requestedCount) and the final Math.min(Math.max(0, reserved), cap) always evaluate to 0. The entire render-worker pool (createWorkerPool, dispatchPass, renderWorkers) is therefore permanently disabled regardless of navigator.hardwareConcurrency; the app silently always falls back to single-threaded rendering on the orchestrator thread, contradicting the UI's "N render workers" display logic and the whole worker-pool infrastructure.
src/main.zig, solidIsDisabled vs src/platform_wasm.zig, solidIsDisabled: the X11 desktop build treats a solid as disabled when phase_state.kind == .disabled or turbidity is non-finite or turbidity >= 0.9, while the WASM build's version only checks phase_state.kind == .disabled. The two platforms therefore diverge in hit-testing/interaction behavior for any turbid (frosted) solid that isn't explicitly given the .disabled kind.
src/raymarcher.zig, solidSdfLocal call to typo.textEngrave3D(local_p, text_slice, lo, cw, ch, he.z): the function signature is textEngrave3D(p, text, text_origin, char_scale, engrave_z, front_z). This call passes cw (label_char_w) as char_scale and ch (label_char_h) as engrave_z (engraving depth). label_char_h is thus never used to control glyph height at all — glyphs are always rendered as squares scaled solely by label_char_w — and instead silently repurposed as the engraving depth into the surface, which is a parameter/semantic mismatch.
src/main.zig, screenToWorld vs renderBand: renderBand samples ray directions at pixel centers, nx = (col + 0.5) / w_f, ny = (row + 0.5) / h_f, but screenToWorld (used for hit-testing/dragging from raw mouse coordinates) computes nx = sx / WIDTH, ny = sy / HEIGHT with no +0.5 pixel-center offset. This produces a systematic half-pixel discrepancy between what is rendered and where mouse clicks/drags are registered.
src/light.zig, KeyLight.sampleBackground: computes light_dir = Vec3.normalize(self.smooth_pos), i.e. it normalizes the light's position vector from the world origin as if it were a direction, rather than computing a direction relative to the actual shading/exit point. The resulting background highlight is independent of where the ray actually exits the scene, only of the light's absolute position coordinates.
src/scene.zig, CausticMap.sample: fully implemented but never called anywhere in the codebase (only sampleBilinear is used) — dead code.
src/sdf.zig, smin: fully implemented but never invoked anywhere in the codebase — dead code.
src/math.zig, hash21, hash31, hash22, Vec2.rotate: implemented but never referenced anywhere else in the provided sources — dead code.
src/optics.zig, OpticalMaterial.abbeNumber, turbiditySpectralScale: implemented but never called anywhere — dead code.
www/index.html: <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg"> references a file that does not exist anywhere in the www/ directory listing — broken/404 resource.
src/platform_wasm.zig: exported functions are inconsistent in how they handle invalid input across the JS/WASM boundary. add_solid and set_drop_activation_radius validate input and return false on failure, but requireSolidIndex (used by set_solid_kind, set_solid_label, get_solid_phase, get_solid_kind, get_solid_pos_x/y, get_solid_half_x/y, get_solid_label_ptr/len) calls std.debug.panic on an out-of-range index, which aborts/traps the entire WASM instance instead of failing gracefully — a single bad index from JS crashes the whole render engine.
www/orchestrator.js: the main thread instantiates the WASM module against the shared WebAssembly.Memory, then createWorkerPool instantiates the same compiled module again in each render worker against the same shared memory. Each WebAssembly.instantiate call re-applies the module's active data segments into linear memory; running this multiple times concurrently against one shared buffer is an unsafe pattern for the module's internal globals (g_frame, g_key_light, etc., which live in linear memory), relying on fragile call-ordering (workers must finish instantiating strictly before init_engine() is called on the main thread) rather than any explicit synchronization.

Line 319: set_solid_label overwrites the existing solid’s label_offset with the offset from a newly initialized temporary OpticalSolid, so changing a label can unintentionally reset or corrupt the label offset.

Line 378: This else branch is dead code because hitTest cannot return a disabled solid.

Line 108: The glyph entry for ASCII 127 is an all-zero dummy/placeholder glyph.
Line 121: Unsupported characters return the finite distance 8.0 instead of std.math.inf(f32), so unsupported characters can incorrectly affect text distance calculations.

Line 138: Empty glyphs return 8.0 instead of std.math.inf(f32), so blank glyphs such as space and DEL produce a finite distance despite containing no filled pixels.

Megerősítem a felsorolt hibák egy részét közvetlenül a fájlból kiolvasott kód alapján, míg néhány állítást — ahol a hivatkozott forrás (x11_bind.c, build.zig, orchestrator.js releváns szakaszai) nem volt közvetlenül elérhető a lekérdezéseimben — nem tudok sem megerősíteni, sem cáfolni.[1]

## Megerősített, valós hibák

A `caustics.zig` `worldToUv` függvényében az Y-tengely valóban ellentétes előjelű a képernyő-világ leképezéssel: `worldToUv` `uv.y = pos.y * 0.5 + 0.5`-t számol, míg `renderBand` a `wy = -(ny * 2.0 - 1.0)` alapján fordítva képezi le a sort világ-Y koordinátára — ez pontosan az általad leírt vertikális tükrözési hiba a caustic térkép és a raymarcher között.[1]

A `platform_wasm.zig`-ben a `requireFinite` ténylegesen `std.debug.panic`-ot hív nem véges értékre, és a `render_band` explicit `@panic("render_band step must be greater than zero")`-t dob step==0 esetén, szemben más exportált függvényekkel (pl. `add_solid`, `set_drop_activation_radius`), amelyek `bool`-lal jeleznek hibát — ez megerősíthető inkonzisztencia a hibakezelésben. Hasonlóképp a `requireSolidIndex` valóban `std.debug.panic`-kal áll le érvénytelen indexre, amit minden index-alapú getter (`get_solid_phase`, `get_solid_kind`, `get_solid_pos_x/y`, `get_solid_half_x/y`, `get_solid_label_ptr/len`) és a `set_solid_kind`/`set_solid_label` is használ — egyetlen rossz index az egész WASM motort megállítja.[1]

A `main.zig` és `platform_wasm.zig` `solidIsDisabled` implementációi ténylegesen eltérnek: az X11-es asztali build `phase_state.kind == .disabled or !std.math.isFinite(turbidity) or turbidity >= 0.9` alapján dönt, míg a WASM verzió kizárólag `phase_state.kind == .disabled`-t vizsgál — ez megerősített platformfüggő viselkedési eltérés zavaros (frosted) szolidoknál.[1]

A `screenToWorld` (`nx = sx / WIDTH`, fél pixeles eltolás nélkül) és a `renderBand` (`nx = (col + 0.5) / w_f`) közötti fél pixeles eltérés is közvetlenül látszik a kódban, tehát valós, rendszeres torzítás a kattintás-regisztráció és a renderelt kép között.[1]

A `light.zig` `sampleBackground` függvényében a `light_dir = Vec3.normalize(self.smooth_pos)` sor szó szerint a fényforrás abszolút világpozícióját normalizálja irányvektorként, nem pedig a tényleges kilépési ponthoz viszonyított irányt (ahogy a helyesen megírt `directionFrom` teszi) — ez egy valódi, azonosítható logikai hiba, amit a kód pontosan alátámaszt.[1]

## Nem megerősíthető állítások

Az X11 `XKeycodeToKeysym` vs. nyers hardver-keycode kérdés (`ev.keycode == 9 or 24`) az `x11_bind.c` tartalmától függ, amit nem sikerült lekérnem ebben a körben — a `platform_x11.zig`-ben látott `pollEvent` csak annyit mutat, hogy `ce.keycode`-ot közvetlenül átveszi, a `refr_poll_event` C-implementációja nélkül nem dönthető el biztosan, hogy keysymet vagy nyers kódot ad vissza. Hasonlóan a `www/orchestrator.js` `MAX_RENDER_WORKERS = 0`, `INITIAL_MEMORY_PAGES`, `chooseWorkerCount`, valamint a `build.zig` `initial_memory` értékei, illetve a `scene.zig` `CausticMap.sample` holt kód állítása és a `sdf.zig`/`math.zig`/`optics.zig` "sosem hívott" függvények listája olyan fájlrészletekre hivatkoznak, amelyeket ez a beszélgetés eddig nem tárt fel teljes egészében számomra — ezeket nem tudom sem megerősíteni, sem hallucináció nélkül cáfolni.[1]

Ha szeretnéd, konkrétan rákereshetek még a `scene.zig`, `sdf.zig`, `x11_bind.c` és `orchestrator.js` releváns szakaszaira, hogy a fennmaradó állításokat is soronként ellenőrizzem.
